pipelines-flush-backpressure.title: Treat PipeWriter.FlushAsync as a backpressure boundary
pipelines-flush-backpressure.short: A flush can asynchronously wait for the reader
pipelines-flush-backpressure.summary: System.IO.Pipelines coordinates producers and consumers; FlushAsync is where a writer can observe completion, cancellation, and pressure from buffered data.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.why: Ignoring the asynchronous flush boundary can let a producer outrun its consumer or mishandle shutdown.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.tips: Await flushes, inspect completion when appropriate, and keep ownership of the writer clear through shutdown.

datetimeoffset-timezone-conversion-bound.title: Separate event instants from time-zone presentation
datetimeoffset-timezone-conversion-bound.short: Persist an instant, convert to local civil time at the boundary
datetimeoffset-timezone-conversion-bound.summary: DateTimeOffset can represent an unambiguous instant while TimeZoneInfo applies regional offset rules for display and scheduling.
datetimeoffset-timezone-conversion-bound.why: Persisting DateTime.Now as if it were universal makes daylight-saving transitions and cross-zone data ambiguous.
datetimeoffset-timezone-conversion-bound.tips: Store instants with an offset or UTC representation and carry the intended time-zone identifier separately when regional rules matter.

socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.title: Understand dual-mode sockets when supporting IPv4 and IPv6
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.short: One IPv6 socket can accept mapped IPv4 endpoints when configured
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.summary: A dual-mode IPv6 socket can reduce duplicated listener logic while still serving IPv4 clients on supported platforms.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.why: Assuming address-family behavior is identical everywhere can cause listeners or endpoint comparisons to fail unexpectedly.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.tips: Choose dual-mode behavior deliberately, test deployment platforms, and normalize endpoint handling where address representation matters.

stream-read-exactly-protocol-records.title: Use exact reads for fixed-size protocol fields
stream-read-exactly-protocol-records.short: Stream reads are allowed to return fewer bytes than requested
stream-read-exactly-protocol-records.summary: ReadExactlyAsync expresses the common requirement that a fixed-size header or record must be filled before parsing.
stream-read-exactly-protocol-records.why: Parsing after one ReadAsync call can consume an incomplete header because streams do not promise to fill the supplied buffer.
stream-read-exactly-protocol-records.tips: Use exact reads for fixed-size records and bounded loops for variable-length bodies, with explicit EOF handling.

source-generated-logging-hot-path.title: Use source-generated logging on measured hot paths
source-generated-logging-hot-path.short: Pre-generate logging code instead of repeatedly parsing templates
source-generated-logging-hot-path.summary: LoggerMessage source generation can reduce logging overhead and allocations while preserving structured fields.
source-generated-logging-hot-path.why: High-frequency logging sites can spend meaningful CPU and allocation budget preparing messages even when application work is small.
source-generated-logging-hot-path.tips: Use it for stable, frequently executed log messages; keep event IDs and field names intentional and benchmark before broad rewrites.

dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.title: Use alternate dictionary lookup to avoid temporary key allocations
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.short: Query compatible key representations without materializing a new key
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.summary: Alternate lookup APIs can let compatible key representations such as spans participate in dictionary lookup without first allocating a temporary object.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.why: Creating a short-lived string for every lookup can dominate allocation in parsing-heavy hot paths.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.tips: Use only when the comparer supports the alternate representation and measurement shows temporary key creation matters.

xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.title: Stream large XML and configure XmlReader for untrusted input
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.short: Avoid unnecessary full-document materialization and unsafe resolver behavior
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.summary: XmlReader provides forward-only XML processing and explicit settings for DTD and external resource handling.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.why: Blindly loading large or untrusted XML can create avoidable memory pressure and unsafe external-resource behavior.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.tips: Disable features you do not need, impose application-level size limits, and process large documents incrementally.

assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.title: Resolve managed and native plugin assets with AssemblyDependencyResolver
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.short: Plugin dependency resolution should follow the plugin's dependency context
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.summary: AssemblyDependencyResolver maps assembly and unmanaged-library names to assets associated with a plugin component.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.why: Searching arbitrary directories manually can select incompatible versions and breaks native dependency resolution easily.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.tips: Pair the resolver with a dedicated AssemblyLoadContext and keep plugin loading policy explicit.

aspnetcore-httpcontext-request-scope-lif.title: Do not let HttpContext or request-scoped services escape the request
aspnetcore-httpcontext-request-scope-lif.short: Request state has a bounded lifetime
aspnetcore-httpcontext-request-scope-lif.summary: HttpContext and services resolved from RequestServices belong to the active ASP.NET Core request scope.
aspnetcore-httpcontext-request-scope-lif.why: Detached background work can run after the request and its scoped services have been disposed.
aspnetcore-httpcontext-request-scope-lif.tips: Await request work in scope or enqueue durable data to a background service that creates its own dependency-injection scope.

unity-managed-allocation-frame-budget.title: Keep recurring managed allocations out of Unity frame loops
unity-managed-allocation-frame-budget.short: Small per-frame allocations accumulate into GC pressure
unity-managed-allocation-frame-budget.summary: LINQ materialization, temporary collections, and repeated strings in Update-like loops can create a steady managed allocation rate.
unity-managed-allocation-frame-budget.why: Even individually small allocations can trigger collections that disturb frame-time consistency.
unity-managed-allocation-frame-budget.tips: Measure with Unity profiling tools, reuse storage where ownership is clear, and move recomputation to meaningful change boundaries.
